summary: ASTRA GUARDIANS is an educational space-defense game in which players become a computer-science-skilled astronaut protecting Earth from potential space-object threats. Players explore near-Earth object observations, analyze asteroid characteristics, and complete interactive missions using science-informed defense strategies. details:
ASTRA GUARDIANS: An Interactive Space Survival and Planetary Defense Game

ASTRA GUARDIANS is an educational space-themed game designed to introduce players to near-Earth objects, planetary defense and the challenges of protecting Earth from potential space hazards. The project places the player in the role of an astronaut and space defender whose mission is to understand incoming cosmic objects and make informed decisions about protecting our planet.

The game incorporates space hazards such as asteroids, comets and other near-Earth objects. Players explore missions, examine information about space objects and learn about different planetary-defense strategies, including early detection, kinetic impact and the proposed gravity tractor technique. The project also incorporates NASA's Near Earth Object Web Service (NeoWs), which provides information about real near-Earth objects and helps connect the educational experience with actual astronomical observations.

How it works: The player progresses through space-defense missions, encounters different space-object scenarios and makes strategic decisions. The game provides feedback to explain the selected defense approach. NASA data is incorporated through an API to provide information about real near-Earth objects, while educational scenarios help players understand how planetary-defense strategies work.

Benefits and intended impact: ASTRA GUARDIANS aims to make space science more engaging and accessible, particularly for students and young learners. It encourages scientific curiosity, strategic thinking, problem-solving and awareness of planetary defense. By combining interactive gameplay with NASA data, it creates an opportunity to learn about near-Earth objects and the importance of monitoring our cosmic environment.

Tools and technologies: The project is developed using HTML for structure, CSS for visual design and JavaScript for interactive functionality and game logic. The NASA NeoWs API is used to retrieve near-Earth-object information. Visual Studio Code is used for development, while GitHub provides source-code hosting and GitHub Pages can be used to publish the playable website.

Creativity and innovation: The central concept combines the excitement of an astronaut-based space adventure with the real-world scientific subject of planetary defense. Rather than presenting astronomical information only through text, the project introduces it through missions, interactive decisions and gameplay. It connects the imaginative experience of defending Earth with real astronomical data and scientific concepts.

Factors considered: The project considers scientific accuracy, educational value, accessibility, usability and responsible presentation of astronomical information. Real near-Earth-object observations are distinguished from fictional training scenarios. In particular, the identification of an object as potentially hazardous does not mean that an Earth impact is predicted. The project is an educational simulation and does not provide operational impact predictions or professional planetary-defense guidance.

ASTRA GUARDIANS ultimately seeks to transform curiosity about space into an engaging learning experience while highlighting the importance of scientific observation, technological innovation and international efforts to understand and protect our planet.
